sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Plate Loaded Shoulder Press Machine is a compound upper body exercise that targets the deltoids, triceps, and upper chest using a plate-loaded machine with a guided movement path.

The back support and fixed pressing path allow you to focus entirely on pressing heavy weight overhead without worrying about stabilization or balance.

This machine is ideal for building shoulder mass and pressing strength, offering a safer alternative to free-weight overhead pressing for heavy loads.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds shoulder size and overhead pressing strength
- Back support reduces lower back strain
- Guided path allows focus on the target muscles
- No spotter required for heavy sets
- Plate-loaded design provides a natural resistance curve
- Easy to perform drop sets by quickly removing plates
- Develops all three heads of the deltoid
- Suitable for all experience levels from beginner to advanced

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids

Secondary: Triceps Brachii, Upper Trapezius, Upper Pectoralis Major, Serratus Anterior

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Adjust the seat height so your hands are just above shoulder height on the handles.
2. Sit with your back firmly pressed against the back support.
3. Plant your feet flat on the floor for stability.
4. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
5. Brace your core before beginning the press.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Brace your core and press your hands above your head.
2. Keep your back pressed firmly into the back support throughout.
3. Press all the way to the top of the motion until your arms are fully straight.
4. Squeeze your shoulders at the top of the movement.
5. Return to the starting position in a controlled manner.
6. Control the weight on the way back down — do not let it drop.
7. Stop when your hands return to just above shoulder height.
8. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Seat too high or too low, shifting the pressing angle
- Not pressing the back firmly into the support
- Using momentum or bouncing at the bottom
- Not fully extending the arms at the top
- Flaring elbows too far out
- Arching the lower back excessively
- Letting the weight drop uncontrolled on the return
- Rushing through reps without control
- Gripping the handles too tightly, causing forearm fatigue

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Plate Loaded Shoulder Press Machine
- Weight Plates (Olympic size)
- Optional: Wrist Wraps for heavy sets
- Recommended: Non-slip footwear

sections.heading: Machine Setup
sections.content:
1. Adjust the seat height so the handles align with just above shoulder level.
2. Load equal weight on both sides of the machine.
3. Ensure all pins and safety mechanisms are secured.
4. Test the range of motion with no weight before loading.
5. If the machine has adjustable handle angles, set to a comfortable position.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Back: Firmly pressed against the back support at all times.
2. Feet: Flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
3. Hands: Gripping handles just above shoulder height.
4. Grip: Overhand, firm but not overly tight.
5. Core: Braced throughout the movement.
6. Head: Neutral position, resting against the pad if available.
7. Shoulders: Down and back at the start.
8. Elbows: In line with the handles, not flared excessively.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Seated Shoulder Press: Free-weight overhead pressing
- Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: Independent arm pressing
- Standing Barbell Overhead Press: Full-body overhead pressing
- Smith Machine Shoulder Press: Guided barbell path
- Cable Shoulder Press: Constant tension pressing
- Selectorized Shoulder Press Machine: Pin-loaded alternative

sections.heading: Shoulder Press Variations
sections.content:
Standard Plate Loaded Press: Classic overhead machine pressing
Single-Arm Press: Unilateral work for imbalance correction
Slow Tempo Press: Controlled eccentric for muscle building
Pause Press: Hold at the bottom for increased difficulty
Partial Rep Press: Top-half reps for lockout strength
Drop Set Press: Remove plates progressively for exhaustion
21s Press: 7 bottom half, 7 top half, 7 full range reps

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Reduce range of motion, lower the weight
Wrist Pain: Use wrist wraps, adjust grip position
Neck Pain: Ensure head is in neutral position, not straining forward
Lower Back Pain: Press back firmly into support, brace core harder
No Plate Loaded Machine: Use dumbbells, barbell, or selectorized machine
Limited Plates: Use resistance bands or lighter dumbbells
Learning Stage: Start with no weight, focus on pressing path and control
